Using (eq:ab), the bracket evaluates to 4c_g∂_t∂_ξa ≠ 0, not 0 as claimed. With the corrected signs (matching the rearranged form of (eq:ab)), the bracket vanishes and the O(eps²) defect bound follows correctly.

issues.title: Sign error in defect decomposition proof of Proposition 2

diagnostic_evidence.quote: equivalent to the norm $\|\cdot\|_{A(\mathbb{R}) \times A(\mathbb{R})}$ uniformly in $\eps,\tau,h$ subject to \eqref{eq:stability}

issues.failure_explanation: The assertion that condition (eq:stability) ensures |γ̃_θ| < max{1,|γ_θ|} is false: at θh = β (i.e. cos(β−θh)=1) one has γ̃_θ = 1 and γ_θ = αω², so |γ̃_θ| = 1 = max{1,|γ_θ|} whenever |α|ω² ≤ 1 (i.e. τ/eps² small). Consequently μ = sup_θ γ̃²/(1+γ²) ≥ 1/(1+α²ω⁴) → 1 as τ/eps² → 0, so no uniform μ < 1 exists and the norm-equivalence constant ‖V(θ)^{-1}‖ ≤ 1/√(2(1−μ)) is not uniformly bounded in eps, τ, h as claimed. The eigenvalue conclusion |λ^±| = 1 survives because γ̃² ≤ 1+γ² still holds, but the uniform norm equivalence does not.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken Lemma (th:stability) and Lemma (lem:stability-cn) to state non-uniform norm equivalence (with the equivalence constant depending on τ/eps²), then re-derive Lemma (lem:stability) with this dependence made explicit and verify that the theorems' uniform error bounds still hold via the initial-error compensation argument.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma (th:stability) and Lemma (lem:stability-cn) falsely claim uniform norm equivalence; Lemma (lem:stability) inherits a non-uniform constant through ‖V^{-1}‖. The theorems' error bounds survive because the O(τ) starting-step error multiplied by the non-uniform constant C₂ ∼ eps²/τ yields O(eps²), but the lemma-level uniformity claims are invalid.
issues.title: Non-uniform norm equivalence claimed in linear stability lemma
issues.why_classification: The uniformity claims in two stability lemmas are false and Lemma (lem:stability)'s constant is wrong, but a contained re-analysis (weakening the lemma and verifying compensation in the theorems) preserves all main error bounds without new global proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims the nonlinear stability bound for the weighted Crank–Nicolson method follows from 'the same arguments' used for the explicit leapfrog method (Lemma lem:stability). However, the leapfrog scheme's nonlinear term λ|p_j^n|²p_j^n is explicit (depends only on the known level n), whereas the Crank–Nicolson scheme's nonlinear term λ(|p_j^{n+1}|²+|p_j^{n-1}|²)breve{p}_j^n/2 involves the unknown p^{n+1} implicitly. In the Fourier-transformed error equation this places e^{n+1} on both sides, requiring an absorption or contraction argument not present in the leapfrog proof. The claimed 'same arguments' do not directly apply.

failure_location.quote: using the same arguments together with Lemma~\ref{lem:stability-cn}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Provide a proof for the implicit Crank–Nicolson nonlinear stability that handles the implicit coupling of e^{n+1} in the nonlinear term, for example by bounding the nonlinear difference and absorbing the e^{n+1} contribution into the left-hand side of the energy estimate (requiring τ small relative to the Lipschitz constant but not involving h or eps).
issues.overall_effect: The claim that the weighted Crank–Nicolson method satisfies the same nonlinear stability bound (and hence the same error bounds as stated in Theorems th:MFE, thm, thm:polarized) without any step-size condition is unsupported; the implicit nonlinear coupling is not handled.
issues.title: Incomplete proof of nonlinear stability for weighted Crank–Nicolson method
issues.why_classification: A contained nontrivial argument (implicit nonlinear absorption in the energy estimate) is needed but no new global proof architecture is required; the claim is likely correct and the main guarantees survive.
